nodes.name: Hydrothermal Ni(OH)₂ synthesis
nodes.procedure: NF (3 cm × 4 cm) was cleaned by ultrasonication in acetone, 1 M HCl, ethanol, and DI water for 5 min each, respectively, and dried naturally. In a typical synthesis, 1 mmol of NiCl₂·6H₂O, 5 mmol of CO(NH₂)₂, and 1.5 mmol of NH₄F were dissolved in 30 mL DI water to form a clear solution and then transferred into a 50 mL Teflon-lined autoclave. The clean NF was immersed in and the autoclave was sealed and maintained at 150°C for 10 h. After cooling down to room temperature naturally, the NF was taken out, washed with DI water several times, and dried in vacuum at 60°C for 6 h to obtain Ni(OH)₂/NF.

nodes.name: Oxygen plasma etching
nodes.procedure: As-prepared Ni(OH)₂/NF was treated with oxygen plasma in a homemade plasma processing system for 20 min. The oxygen flow rate was 5 sccm (partial pressure of 9 Pa) with power settings at 150 W.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows uniform nanosheets array after electrochemical doping of Fe/Mo.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After potential cycling in KOH solution containing Fe3+/MoO42-, the broken nanosheets were reconstituted and completely recovered to uniform nanosheets array (Figure 1d; Figure S1c, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows smooth and complete surface with NiOOH phase dominating the nanosheet (0.270 nm inter-planar distance for Ni(OH)2 (100), NiOOH (002) and (110) planes), with embedded NiO clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM image of Ni(OH)2/NF precursor in Figure 1e shows the clear lattice stripes of 0.270 nm inter-planar distance, corresponding to the (100) of Ni(OH)2... Two types of lattice stripes were observed, where NiOOH phase (PDF No. 06-0141) dominates the nanosheet while some tiny NiO clusters embedded.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern further confirms the high crystallinity of these nanosheets... Meanwhile, the clear diffraction patterns representing (002) and (110) planes of NiOOH can be observed in the SAED pattern (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms NiOOH phase (PDF No. 06-0141) formation with strong signals and weak NiO diffraction peaks in p-NiFeMo/NF; (001) peak shifts to lower angle indicating expanded c-direction lattice spacing due to MoO42- insertion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In p-NiFeMo/NF pattern, NiOOH phase (PDF No. 06-0141) forms with strong signals, and weak diffraction peak from remained NiO domains is also observable... the diffraction peak of (001) plane of NiOOH in p-NiFeMo/NF shifts to lower angle compared to that of p-Ni/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, and Mo elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS elemental mapping images display that Ni, Fe, and Mo elements are uniformly distributed in p-NiFeMo/NF (Figure 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows atomic abundance of Fe (5.2%) and Mo (2.5%) in all metals of the nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic abundance of Fe and Mo in all metals of the nanosheets is 5.2% and 2.5%, respectively according to ICP-OES measurements.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Mo-O stretching modes at 825 and 913 cm⁻¹ confirming MoO₄²⁻ presence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Raman spectrum of p-NiFeMo/NF (Figure 2c), the peaks at 825 and 913 cm⁻¹ are assigned to the Mo-O stretching mode from MoO₄²⁻.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS shows increased Ni³⁺ content confirming NiOOH phase formation in p-NiFeMo/NF; O 1s shows increased hydroxide signal after electrochemical doping indicating oxyhydroxide reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The content of Ni³⁺ increases continuously after the electrochemical doping process due to the formation of NiOOH phase for p-NiFeMo/NF... After electrochemical doping, the signal intensity from hydroxide group increases but the intensity from metal-oxygen decreases.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows ν/δ ratio (560/480 cm⁻¹) increases with Fe³⁺/MoO₄²⁻ indicating higher β-NiOOH proportion; post-OER ν/δ = 0.81 confirms highest β/γ ratio stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ν/δ value of p-Ni(OH)₂ increases obviously in the presence of Fe³⁺/MoO₄²⁻ ions... the ν/δ value of p-NiFeMo/NF (0.81) is still higher than that of NiFeMo/NF (0.73).

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl = 3.8 mF cm⁻² indicating larger ECSA compared to Ni(OH)₂/NF (1.7 mF cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl of p-NiFeMo/NF is 3.8 mF cm⁻², considerably larger than Ni(OH)₂/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows smallest charge transfer resistance Rct at 1.526 V indicating fastest OER kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: charge transfer resistance (Rct) of p-NiFeMo/NF is the smallest at the potential of 1.526 V.
